In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of surfactants is an effective treatment for neonatal RDS, and that the use of animal-derived surfactants is superior to the use of synthetic surfactants.

the use of surfactant is not only safe but also effective in reducing the need for mechanical ventilation, the incidence of bronchopulmonary dysplasia and death, and in improving the long-term neurodevelopmental outcome in infants with RDS.
there is a strong association between the use of surfactants and improved outcome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
surfactants are used more often in Poland than in Western Europe.
we are not using enough surfactant in the first minutes of life.
the results of the first Polish survey of the use of surfactants in daily practice show that surfactant treatment is still underutilized.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many different strategies of using surfactant in the treatment of RDS in the neonatal intensive care units in Poland.
the majority of the Polish population has a poor knowledge about the use of surfactants and the most of the respondents do not use them in their daily practice.
the use of surfactants for the treatment of RDS is not uniform across Poland.
